newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy car market seen in crisis, incentives needed.
newsitem.headline: Italy car market seen in crisis, incentives needed.

text.p: Latest Italian car sales data confirm the domestic market is suffering a serious crisis which will not likely be overcome in the short to medium term without measures to encourage demand, a leading sector research body said.
Official figures published on Tuesday showed Italian new car registrations fell 7.5 percent to 74,000 units in August compared with August 1995.

"The high cost for Italy of the difficulties of the car sector, both on a jobs and tax revenue level, fully justify the adoption of measures to support car demand like those which have been introduced successfully in other European countries," the Bologna-based Centro Studi Promotor (CSP) said.
According to CSP, 77 percent of dealers polled in August reported low levels of orders and forecasts for the next three to four months tended to be pessimistic.

The Italian association of Fiat dealers UCIF said in a separate statement that they were worried about the situation and urged the government to take measures to boost the turnover of old for new vehicles.

One way would be to impose more frequent obligatory safety checkups on vehicles, from every five years currently, and to simplify the lengthy, complex and "absurd legislation" covering the registration and sale or purchase of a vehicle, it said.
